findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96` — `await prisma.credential.update({...})` with no `@calcom/prisma` import anywhere in the file (imports lines 1–20). TS2304 at build; `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` on every Salesforce client construction. Confidence 95–100.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97-101` — `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` then `data: { key }`. The helper returns the zod safeParse **wrapper**; every other call site uses `.data` (office365 :264, salesforce :98). Stores `{"success":true,"data":{...}}` into `credential.key`; next `googleCredentialSchema.parse` throws → Google credential permanently bricked, in-place, no backfill. Confidence 90–100.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11` — `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` both evaluate to the literal key `"[object Object]"`; second overwrites first. Schema is effectively `{access_token: string}`. Zod strips unknown keys → in sync mode `refresh_token`/`expiry_date`/`expires_in`/`instance_url`/`scope` are all discarded before being written to `credential.key`. The two comments describe behavior the code does not implement. Confidence 75–90.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-18` — sync branch returns a raw `fetch` `Response`, fallback returns the SDK object; return type is `any`. Google (`CalendarService.ts:94` `const token = res?.data` → `undefined` → TypeError, swallowed by the non-`invalid_grant` catch) and HubSpot (`:177` casts `Response as HubspotToken`, writes `NaN`/`undefined` into the key) both break. Lark/o365/webex work only by coincidence of shape. The headline feature is non-functional for its two biggest apps. Confidence 85–90.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29` — `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`: if the secret is unset and the header absent, `undefined !== undefined` is false and auth passes. `.env.example:236` ships `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET=""` as the default. Comparison also non-constant-time, no rate limit. Endpoint writes arbitrary OAuth credentials for an arbitrary `userId` (:62-91). Confidence 75/100.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30-59` — `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam({ teamId: state?.teamId ?? null, userId })` sits on the branch reachable only when `state?.teamId` is falsy, so it always runs with `teamId: null`. The team-credential path checks only `members.some({userId, accepted: true})` — any ordinary member can install/overwrite team-wide OAuth credentials. `select: { members: ... }` is fetched and unused. Confidence 85–100.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:5-11` / `decodeOAuthState.ts:9` — state is echoed from the client's own query string, unsigned, no nonce, no session binding, then trusted for `teamId`/`returnTo` on return. CSRF → attacker's OAuth account bound as the victim's team credential (compounds with the dead admin check). `encodeOAuthState` is a pure `JSON.parse`→`JSON.stringify` identity no-op despite its name. Confidence 90.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14` — outbound POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends no `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` header despite `.env.example` documenting it as the shared secret. The receiver cannot authenticate Cal.com; anyone reaching it can POST an arbitrary `calcomUserId`/`appSlug` and harvest live access tokens. Confidence 70.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-107` — unconditional token refresh + DB write on **every** `getClient()`/construction (no expiry check), then the returned `jsforce.Connection` uses the pre-refresh `credentialKey.access_token`. Refresh is pure overhead + write amplification + OAuth rate-limit cliff proportional to traffic. Also bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens` entirely (raw `fetch` to login.salesforce.com), so Salesforce never consults the sync endpoint while still validating against the relaxed sync schema. Confidence 80–90.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-80` — `findFirst({where:{userId, appId}})` with no `orderBy` and no `@@unique([userId, appId])`. Concurrent deliveries both miss and both `create`; with multiple connected accounts an arbitrary row's key is overwritten with another account's tokens. `invalid` is not reset to `false` on update. Comment "Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id" treats the missing invariant as immutable. Confidence 85.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27` — `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` fires unconditionally (outside the sharing-flag branch) and, because the real token was just stripped, always. The literal string is persisted as the credential's refresh token; next refresh sends garbage to the provider. o365 `:264-272` spread overwrites the row's real refresh token with it. Confidence 85–100.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15` — no timeout, no `response.ok` check, no fallback to `refreshFunction()`. A single self-hosted endpoint becomes a hard sync dependency on the refresh path of every calendar/video integration; a hang stalls every booking/availability fetch (Node fetch has no default timeout). Confidence 85.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:41-67` — both branches unconditionally `create`, never upsert. Every reconnect leaves an orphan row with a revoked refresh token; combined with the unordered `findFirst` the webhook may keep updating the stale orphan. Confidence 75.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264-281` — `expires_in` is transformed to an absolute epoch under the same key name; in sharing mode the minimum schema never yields it, so the stale value survives, `isExpired()` is permanently true, and every calendar call triggers a refresh + destructive `credential.update`. Confidence 75.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57-59,78,85` — `keys` typed as opaque `z.string()`; the decrypted object replaces a working `credential.key` with zero shape validation against the app's credential schema. No migration, no rollback: findings above mutate keys in place on the hot path, and a rolling deploy has old and new pods writing incompatible key shapes to the same rows. Confidence 85.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86` — `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError({statusCode: 400, message: response.statusText})`. undici returns `statusText: ""` over HTTP/2, so this throws on successful refreshes with an empty message. Should be `!response.ok`. Confidence 75–80.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:42,50` — selects `slug` then indexes `appStoreMetadata[app.slug as keyof typeof appStoreMetadata]`, but that map is keyed by **dirName** (`googlecalendar`), not hyphenated slug (`google-calendar`). The cast suppresses the type error; at runtime `appMetadata` is `undefined` → always 404 for exactly the multi-word apps this feature targets. Confidence 75.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-265` + `salesforce:92-94` — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` now throws on parse failure, so the retained `tokenResponse.success &&` and `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` guards are dead code. apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17-32,57-59` — no `req.method` guard (GET/PUT/DELETE all reach the write path); `.parse` not `safeParse` → ZodError as a 500 with stack instead of 400; unguarded `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse`; `|| ""` silently accepts a missing `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. App slugs are bare magic strings duplicated across two subsystems with no shared source of truth — `googlecalendar:90` `"google-calendar"`, `hubspot:186`, `office365calendar:258`, `office365video:72` `"msteams"`, `larkcalendar:76`, `webex:75` — and are the join key against `appId: appMetadata.slug` written at `app-credential.ts:87`. packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17` — `WEBAPP_URL + \`/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback\`` replaces `${appConfig.slug}` while `appConfig` is still used at :12 and :22. Unrelated to the task; second source of truth for the slug. Confidence 100.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the object literal uses computed property names `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. `z.string()` returns a ZodString object, whose `.toString()` results in a constant string (effectively `"[object Object]"`), so both computed keys collide and the latter overwrites the former in the JS object literal. As a result, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` does not implement “any numeric property is expiry” nor “allow other properties”; it’s essentially `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() })`. Since `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, in the sync-path (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) fields like `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, `instance_url`, etc. will be discarded when safeParsed, contradicting the comments and likely breaking token persistence/update logic.

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler authenticates solely via `req.headers[headerName] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. In Node/Next, missing headers resolve to `undefined`, and if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is also `undefined` (unset) then `undefined !== undefined` is false, so the 403 is not triggered and the request is accepted. Additionally, `.env.example` introduces `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET=""` as a default; if a deploy copies this (empty string), an attacker may be able to send the header with an empty value (e.g. `calcom-webhook-secret:`) which would compare equal and bypass auth. Once past this check, the endpoint can create/update credentials for any `userId` supplied in the body (writes to `prisma.credential.update/create`), making the bypass impact severe. The constant-time/rate-limit comments are more general, but the auth-bypass logic is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-107` — unconditional token refresh + DB write on **every** `getClient()`/construction (no expiry check), then the returned `jsforce.Connection` uses the pre-refresh `credentialKey.access_token`. The candidate adds extra concerns (unconditional refresh, rate limiting), but the central issue matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-80` — `findFirst({where:{userId, appId}})` with no `orderBy` and no `@@unique([userId, appId])`. This is verifiably present in the diff and can race under concurrent webhook deliveries for the same `(userId, appId)`: both requests can observe “no row” and both attempt `create`, leading either to duplicate rows (if no DB uniqueness) or a thrown unique-constraint error (if there is one) with no error handling. The finding’s additional claims about the absence of an `@@unique([userId, appId])`, overwriting an “arbitrary row” due to multiple connected accounts, and not resetting an `invalid` flag cannot be verified from this diff because the Prisma schema/model fields and constraints are not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15` — no timeout, no `response.ok` check, no fallback to `refreshFunction()`. A single self-hosted endpoint becomes a hard sync dependency on the refresh path of every calendar/video integration; a hang stalls every booking/availability fetch (Node fetch has no default timeout). Confidence 85.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, the code unconditionally does a `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: ... })` and immediately returns that response. There is (1) no timeout/AbortController, so a hanging endpoint can hang the refresh path because Node/undici `fetch` has no default timeout; (2) no `response.ok`/status handling before returning; and (3) no fallback to `refreshFunction()` on network failure or non-2xx. This makes the external sync endpoint a hard dependency for token refresh in the enabled configuration (user credentials), which is a real reliability/correctness issue introduced by the diff.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57-59,78,85` — `keys` typed as opaque `z.string()`; the decrypted object replaces a working `credential.key` with zero shape validation against the app's credential schema. adjudication.rationale: The webhook handler validates `req.body.keys` only as an opaque `z.string()` (encrypted blob). After decryption it does `JSON.parse(...)` and writes the resulting value directly into `credential.key` (`prisma.credential.update/create`) without validating that the decrypted object matches the expected credential schema for the target app. This is verifiable in the diff: there is no app-specific zod parse/check before persisting. That can persist malformed/incompatible credential shapes and break downstream code that assumes a specific key structure. (The “rolling deploy” aspect is more speculative, but the lack of schema validation and in-place mutation of `credential.key` is a real correctness risk introduced here.)
